text: Somebody always fronts the money.\NThen spends a week chasing five people for $45.
You write the rule in your own words.\NNothing in the code reads it.
It sets the split, the recipient and the deadline.
One decision. Ten real PayPal calls.
Then it sleeps. A routine payment is recorded by code\Nand never wakes it — waiting costs nothing.
$135 of $180. Two people still haven't paid.
It woke up, chose who to chase,\Nand wrote the nudge itself.
$135 collected. $45 short.\NNobody is going to decide this but the agent.
It quotes the organizer back, and attests the numbers\Nagainst PayPal before a cent moves.
One batch. Three refunds,\Neach exactly what that person paid.
In $135. Out $135. Delta $0.00.\NEveryone got back exactly what they put in.
“Refund everyone unless all five of us actually chip in.”\NA count of people — not an amount.
$180 collected, four of five paid.\NThe agent gives it all back.
No if-statement could have done that.
